messages:
tyler: Heads-up — ran into a concurrency/cancelation footgun in a tiny sample that mixes generator streams + auth refresh. Repro is small and flaky.

jia: Oof. Can you paste the snippet and the failure mode?

tyler: Using the quickstart loop `for gen.Next()` and a parent ctx with timeout. When token refresh kicks in the transport reconnects and occasionally the app either: a) leaks a goroutine, b) gets a vague EOF, or c) sees Close() return a nil-pointer panic on older releases.

tyler: Minimal repro:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
gen, _ := client.Generator(ctx, model, nil)
// simple loop from quickstart
for gen.Next() {
  fmt.Print(gen.Value().Text)
}
if err := gen.Err(); err != nil {
  log.Printf("gen err=%v", err)
}
_ = gen.Close()
```

frank: Key UX issue: Next() is not cancellation-friendly — callers have to invent patterns (goroutine/select) to ensure the loop exits on ctx cancel. And Close() used to not be idempotent.

jia: Two small API proposals to address this with minimal churn: 1) Add an iteration helper that accepts a ctx at the call-site so cancel is explicit, e.g. `gen.NextContext(ctx)` or `gen.NextWith(ctx)`. 2) Make Close() idempotent and introduce well-known error sentinel values: `ErrCanceled`, `ErrTransient` (or `ErrRetryable`), and `ErrClosed`.

tyler: I prototyped a tiny adapter in the samples repo: `sdk/iteradapter` which exposes `IterChan(gen, ctx)` returning a receive-only channel you can range over; it handles ctx and Close() for you. Example sample in the repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk-samples/tree/main/iteradapter.

frank: Love the adapter idea for samples, but for the core SDK I'd prefer `NextWith(ctx)` — small surface area and idiomatic. Implementation: select on user ctx vs internal message channel in the generator recv path. On ctx cancel set Err() to context.Canceled and return false. For transport/auth transient failures surface ErrTransient so apps can choose to resume vs recreate the generator.

jia: Agree. Also add a guarantee: Close() never panics and is safe to call from multiple goroutines (use sync.Once internally). Add unit tests that simulate token rotation (auth middleware returns 401 twice then 200) and assert runtime.NumGoroutine delta == 0 after client.Close().

tyler: UX note for docs: show two patterns — small apps should use the IterChan helper; production systems that need tighter control should use `for gen.NextWith(ctx)` + check `errors.Is(gen.Err(), sdk.ErrTransient)` to decide whether to retry. Add a code snippet in quickstart showing both.

jia: Also add a short migration blurb: if you currently rely on `for gen.Next()` + manual goroutine cancels, change to `for gen.NextWith(ctx)` and `defer gen.Close()`; or copy the IterChan helper. That will remove ~70% of our support tickets.

frank: I'll open a PR that: - adds NextWith(ctx) (stable alias NextContext if maintainers prefer) - makes Close idempotent - exports ErrTransient/ErrCanceled/ErrClosed - adds an IterChan helper in samples - adds unit tests for auth rotation and goroutine leak detection. PR link when ready.

eng-qa-bot: queued tests for branch gen-nextwith-iteradapter (run 1/3). Suggested stress run: 5k iterations with auth-proxy toggling 401/200 to catch flakiness.

tyler: Thanks all. If we land this, let's update the quickstart and the sample app used in the onboarding flow. I can help write the sample text and the migration note. :rocket:
